module_title: Simple Oil Extraction Methods for Small-Scale Production

lessons.title: Steam Distillation Using a Cooking Pot and Local Materials
lessons.body: You can build a working steam distillation setup with a large cooking pot (at least 20 litres), a lid, a length of copper or stainless steel tubing (about 1 metre of 6â8 mm diameter), a heat source (firewood, charcoal, or gas), and a bucket of cold water. First, place your plant materialâchopped lemongrass, eucalyptus leaves, or tea tree branchesâon a rack or sieve inside the pot so it sits above the water. Add water until it is just below the rack. Put the lid on upside down so the handle acts as a collection point, or drill a hole in the lid and insert the tubing. Seal gaps with dough made from flour and water. As the water boils, steam passes through the plant material, vaporising the essential oil. The steam and oil vapour travel through the tubing, which you run through a bucket of cold water (the condenser). The cold water causes the vapour to condense back into liquid, which drips into a receiving jar. For lemongrass, use 1 kg of fresh chopped leaves per 5 litres of water. For eucalyptus, 1 kg of leaves per 4 litres. For tea tree, 1.5 kg of leaves per 5 litres. Distillation takes 1â2 hours. Collect about 500 ml of distillate; the oil will float or sink depending on density. Siphon off the oil layer with a small syringe or separate it using a separatory funnel made from a clear plastic bottle. Expect yields of 0.5â1% for lemongrass, 0.8â1.5% for eucalyptus, and 0.6â1.2% for tea tree. Keep the fire steadyâtoo hot and you may burn the plant material; too cool and distillation stalls. This method works in rural areas with no electricity.

lessons.title: Cold Pressing for Lemongrass: A Step-by-Step Guide
lessons.body: Cold pressing is best for lemongrass because heat can damage the delicate citrus-like oils. You need fresh lemongrass stalks (not dried), a strong knife or machete, a clean stone or wooden pounding block, a manual press (or a heavy stone), a clean cloth (muslin or cheesecloth), and a glass jar. Harvest lemongrass early in the morning when oil content is highest. Cut the stalks about 10 cm above the ground. Remove the outer dry leaves and roots. Chop the stalks into 5â10 cm pieces. You will need about 2 kg of fresh stalks to get 10â20 ml of oil. Pound the pieces with a stone or wooden mallet until they are bruised and fibrousâthis breaks the oil cells. Do not reduce to a paste; just crush them well. Place the crushed lemongrass in a clean cloth and twist it tightly to squeeze out the juice. Collect the greenish liquid in a jar. Let it stand for 2â4 hours. The essential oil will separate and float on top of the water. Use a small syringe or a spoon to skim off the oil layer. You can also pour the liquid into a narrow-necked bottle and use a pipette to remove the top oil. For better yield, repeat the pressing with the same pulp after adding a little clean water, then separate again. Yields are lowâabout 0.5â1 ml of oil per kg of fresh stalksâso cold pressing is best for small batches or for making fresh lemongrass oil for immediate use. Store the oil in a dark glass bottle in a cool place. Cold pressing preserves the fresh, lemony aroma that steam distillation can sometimes alter.

lessons.title: Solar Distillation: Using the African Sun to Extract Oils
lessons.body: Solar distillation uses the sunâs heat to evaporate water and essential oils from plant material, then condenses them. You need a clear plastic sheet (UV-resistant, 2â3 metres), a large black pot or basin, a smaller collection container, a stone or weight, and a sunny spot. Dig a hole in the ground about 1 metre wide and 50 cm deep. Place the black pot in the centre filled with water and plant materialâuse 500 g of chopped lemongrass or eucalyptus leaves per 2 litres of water. Put the collection container in the middle of the pot, raised so it doesnât touch the water. Cover the hole with the plastic sheet, sealing the edges with soil or stones. Place a small stone in the centre of the plastic so it dips slightly over the collection container. The sun heats the pot, water evaporates, and oil vapours rise. They condense on the cooler plastic and run down into the collection container. This works best in hot, dry climates with full sun. Start early in the morning and collect in the late afternoon. Expect 100â200 ml of distillate per day, containing a small amount of oil. For better yield, use a solar still with a slanted glass cover and a separate condenser. You can also use a black hose coiled in a box with a glass lidâthe sun heats the hose, and steam travels through it, condensing at the end. Solar distillation is slow and yields less oil than steam distillation, but it requires no fuel and works in remote areas. Use it for lemongrass and eucalyptus; tea tree may need higher temperatures. Separate the oil layer with a syringe after letting the distillate stand.

lessons.title: Solvent Extraction with Cheap Local Solvents
lessons.body: Solvent extraction uses a chemical to pull oil from plant material. For small-scale, use food-grade ethanol (available as strong drinking alcohol or from chemical suppliers) or hexane (from hardware stores as a cleaning solvent). Avoid methanol or petrolâthey are toxic. You need 1 kg of dried, ground plant material (lemongrass, eucalyptus, or tea tree), 2â3 litres of solvent, a large glass jar with a lid, a cloth for filtering, and a heat source for evaporating the solvent. Place the plant material in the jar and cover with solvent. Seal and shake well. Let it soak for 24â48 hours, shaking occasionally. Strain through a cloth into another jar. Repeat the soaking with fresh solvent on the same plant material two more times to get all the oil. Combine all the solvent extracts. Now you must remove the solvent. For ethanol, you can evaporate it by placing the jar in a warm water bath (50â60Â°C) outdoors or in a well-ventilated area. Ethanol evaporates first, leaving the essential oil and some plant waxes. For hexane, you need a still or careful heatingâhexane is flammable, so do this outside, away from flames. After evaporation, you will have a thick, dark oil called a concrete or absolute. It contains essential oil plus waxes and pigments. To purify, mix the concrete with ethanol, chill it, and filter out the waxes, then evaporate the ethanol again. Yields are higher than steam distillation: 1â3% for lemongrass, 2â4% for eucalyptus. But solvent extraction is more dangerous and requires careful ventilation. Only use this method if you cannot get a steam distillation setup.

lessons.title: Filtering and Purifying Your Oil Without Expensive Equipment
lessons.body: After extraction, your oil may contain water, plant particles, waxes, or other impurities. Filtering and purifying improve quality and shelf life. Start with a simple gravity filter: place a funnel lined with a coffee filter, clean cotton cloth, or blotting paper. Pour your oil through it. For faster filtering, use a clean plastic bottle with the bottom cut off, packed with clean sand and a cloth at the neck. Pour the oil through the sand; it traps particles. If your oil contains water, let it stand in a narrow-necked bottle for 24 hours. The oil will separate and float (or sink). Use a syringe or pipette to remove the oil layer. For lemongrass and eucalyptus, oil floats; for tea tree, it may sink. To remove waxes, chill the oil in a refrigerator or in a bucket of ice water for 2â3 hours. Waxes solidify and can be scraped off or filtered out. For deeper purification, mix the oil with an equal volume of warm water (60Â°C), shake well, and let separate. Repeat 2â3 times. This removes water-soluble impurities. Then add a small amount of anhydrous sodium sulfate (available from chemical suppliers) or dry sand to absorb remaining water. Stir and filter again. If you want to remove colour, pass the oil through activated charcoal (from water filters) packed in a cloth. But note: charcoal may also remove some aroma. For most small-scale producers, simple filtering and water separation are enough. Store the purified oil in a dark glass bottle with a tight lid. Proper filtering prevents spoilage and makes your oil more marketable.

lessons.title: Storing Your Oil to Prevent Spoilage in Hot Climates
lessons.body: Essential oils can spoil if exposed to heat, light, and oxygen. In hot African climates, you must store them carefully. Use dark glass bottles (amber or cobalt blue) with tight-fitting caps. Plastic bottles can absorb oil and degrade; avoid them for long-term storage. Fill bottles almost to the top to reduce air spaceâoxygen causes oxidation. Store in a cool, dark place: a cellar, a shaded cupboard, or even a hole in the ground lined with a box. Ideal temperature is below 25Â°C; if your area is hotter, consider a small solar-powered fridge or a clay pot cooler (zeer pot). Keep away from sunlightâUV light breaks down oils. For lemongrass and tea tree, which are prone to oxidation, add a few drops of vitamin E oil (if available) as an antioxidant. You can also purge the bottle with nitrogen or use a vacuum sealer, but these are optional. Label each bottle with the oil name, date, and method of extraction. Use within 1â2 years for best quality; citrus oils like lemongrass last 1 year, eucalyptus 2â3 years, tea tree 1â2 years. Check for spoilage: a rancid, sour, or thick smell means discard. To extend shelf life, store oils in smaller bottles and only open the one you are using. For transport to market, wrap bottles in cloth and keep them in a cool box. Never store oils near strong-smelling items like onions or petrolâthey absorb odours. Following these steps will keep your oil fresh and sellable even in the hottest months.

quiz.q: What is the recommended ratio of fresh lemongrass leaves to water for steam distillation?
options: A) 1 kg leaves to 5 litres water
B) 2 kg leaves to 1 litre water
C) 500 g leaves to 10 litres water
D) 1 kg leaves to 2 litres water
quiz.explanation: The lesson states 1 kg of fresh chopped lemongrass leaves per 5 litres of water.

quiz.q: Which material is NOT recommended for building a steam distillation condenser?
quiz.explanation: Plastic hose may melt or release chemicals; copper or stainless steel is recommended.

quiz.q: What is the expected oil yield from steam distillation of eucalyptus leaves?
quiz.explanation: The lesson gives 0.8â1.5% yield for eucalyptus.

quiz.q: In cold pressing lemongrass, why should you avoid drying the stalks?
options: A) Dried stalks are harder to pound
B) Fresh stalks contain more oil
C) Dried stalks produce toxic oil
quiz.explanation: Fresh lemongrass has higher oil content; drying reduces yield.

quiz.q: How long should you let the cold-pressed lemongrass juice stand to separate oil?
quiz.explanation: The lesson says to let it stand for 2â4 hours for oil separation.

quiz.q: What is the typical yield of cold-pressed lemongrass oil per kg of fresh stalks?
quiz.explanation: The lesson states 0.5â1 ml of oil per kg of fresh stalks.

quiz.q: In solar distillation, what is the purpose of the black pot?
options: B) To absorb heat and evaporate water
quiz.explanation: The black pot absorbs solar heat, speeding evaporation.

quiz.q: How much plant material is recommended for a solar still using a 2-litre water pot?
quiz.explanation: The lesson says 500 g of chopped plant material per 2 litres of water.

quiz.q: Which of these is a safe solvent for small-scale essential oil extraction?
quiz.explanation: Food-grade ethanol is safe; methanol and petrol are toxic.

quiz.q: How long should plant material soak in solvent during solvent extraction?
quiz.explanation: The lesson recommends soaking for 24â48 hours, shaking occasionally.

quiz.q: What is the main danger of using hexane as a solvent?
options: B) It is flammable and toxic
quiz.explanation: Hexane is flammable and must be used with ventilation, away from flames.

quiz.q: After solvent extraction, what is the thick dark oil called?
quiz.explanation: The lesson calls it a concrete or absolute; concrete is the initial thick oil.

quiz.q: Which method can remove water-soluble impurities from essential oil?
quiz.explanation: Washing with warm water (60Â°C) and separating removes water-soluble impurities.

quiz.q: What does chilling essential oil in a refrigerator help remove?
quiz.explanation: Chilling solidifies waxes, which can then be filtered out.

quiz.q: Which material can be used to absorb remaining water from oil?
quiz.explanation: Anhydrous sodium sulfate absorbs water; salt may not be as effective.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid using activated charcoal to purify essential oil?
quiz.explanation: Charcoal can adsorb aromatic compounds, reducing oil quality.

quiz.q: What type of bottle is best for storing essential oils?
quiz.explanation: Dark glass protects oil from light and reduces oxidation.

quiz.q: Why should you fill storage bottles almost to the top?
options: B) To reduce air space and oxidation
quiz.explanation: Less air means less oxygen, slowing oxidation.

quiz.q: What is a zeer pot used for?
quiz.explanation: A zeer pot is a clay pot cooler for storing oils in hot climates.

quiz.q: Which essential oil has the shortest shelf life according to the lesson?
quiz.explanation: Lemongrass lasts about 1 year, shorter than eucalyptus and tea tree.

quiz.q: What is a sign that essential oil has spoiled?
options: B) It becomes thicker and rancid
C) It changes colour to clear
quiz.explanation: Rancid, sour, or thick smell indicates spoilage.

quiz.q: How can you extend the shelf life of lemongrass oil?
quiz.explanation: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, slowing oxidation.

quiz.q: In steam distillation, why is the lid placed upside down or with a hole?
quiz.explanation: The inverted lid or hole directs vapour into the condenser for collection.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of sealing gaps in the distillation pot with dough?
options: C) To make it airtight for safety
quiz.explanation: Dough seals gaps so steam only exits through the condenser.

quiz.q: How long does steam distillation typically take for lemongrass?
quiz.explanation: The lesson states 1â2 hours for distillation.

quiz.q: In cold pressing, why should you pound the lemongrass instead of grinding to a paste?
options: B) To break oil cells without making separation hard
quiz.explanation: Pounding bruises the stalks, releasing oil without creating a paste that traps oil.

quiz.q: What can be used as a simple solar still cover?
quiz.explanation: Clear plastic sheet allows sunlight in and condenses vapour.

quiz.q: Why is solar distillation less efficient than steam distillation?
options: B) It depends on sun and is slow
D) It only works at night
quiz.explanation: Solar distillation is slow and yields less oil due to lower temperatures.

quiz.q: What should you do after solvent extraction to remove ethanol?
options: B) Evaporate in warm water bath
quiz.explanation: Evaporating ethanol in a warm water bath (50â60Â°C) is safe and effective.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a recommended filtering material for essential oil?
quiz.explanation: Plastic mesh may not trap fine particles and can react with oil.
